And the common people, the inhabitants of Jazīra, gathered against him,
and they wanted to kill him,
and with difficulty he escaped and fled.
And that Sayf al-Dīn gathered the Christians and imprisoned them,
while demanding from them two thousand gold dinars;
and it was the day of the Ascension.
And those Christians remained in prison,
having lost hope of their lives.
And Sayf al-Dīn distributed much gold to the troops,
and about seventy thousand Kurds gathered to him,
and they took him and brought him to Syria.
When Jazīra was left without a ruler,
two men, guards {OCR?}, leaped up,
the name of one was 'Izzāz Bās,
and the other Muhammad, chief of the guard;
and they made themselves rulers.
And they brought the Christians out of prison after taking seven hundred dinars from them,
and they killed only two of them, who used to go and come to the Tatars.
And at that time, 'Izz al-Dīn Aybak,
the lord of 'Imādīyah,
the slave of Badr al-Dīn {OCR?}, gathered
about three thousand horsemen,
and came to reign over Jazīra.
And Nūrīn the emir met them {OCR?}
with three hundred horsemen by the River Dibsha which descends from the mountains of Qardū,
and broke him and put him to flight.
And also 'Abdallāh, who ruled over Mayperqāt,
once came to take it,
and was not able to.
And at the end of the summer of this year,
Sultan 'Izz al-Dīn of Iconium prepared himself to go to pay homage to the king of kings,
because he was being pressed by envoys.
And when they pitched his tents outside Iconium in order to set out,
a spy arrived and said to him:
"Alyāqāq Noyan has arrived at Aqsarā,
and with him Rukn al-Dīn your brother and the Parwāna,
and they are prepared, as soon as they meet you, to bind you,
and in chains bring you to the king of kings."
And he was terrified, and left his tent-curtains while they were still pitched,
and took his sons and his household, and fled to Constantinople to Michael, king of the Greeks.
